<!-- pr-reviewer: 79c7c909a9c134939fe845de730f5dab8c581f08 -->

Ready for the maintainer to merge.

This is a delta review of `79c7c909a` against the reviewed head `418e88034` (review of PR #3651). The pin was verified there. This run checks the clippy fix.

**What looks good**
- The delta is only the helper signature and its call sites. `tilted_wall` becomes `fn tilted_wall(spec: TiltedWall) -> Vec<Triangle>` with a `struct TiltedWall` at `crates/motion/src/drilling/tests_tilted.rs:14`, and each call site passes the same field values. The other hunks rewrap existing `assert!` calls for rustfmt; a whitespace-insensitive `git diff -w 418e88034 79c7c909a` shows no condition, message, fixture, degree, band, thickness or tolerance change.
- The mutation proof from `418e88034` stands. The assertions are byte-for-byte the same condition, and `recognize::FIT_TOL` is untouched, so the recorded result still holds: `FIT_TOL` 0.02 -> 0.5 made `tilted_holes_in_a_plate_are_not_drilled_along_z` fail at `tests_tilted.rs:81` with the 2 and 5 degree `Hole` values, and the file was restored byte-identical. I did not re-run it, because this diff cannot reach that behaviour.
- The clippy blocker is gone. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` exits 0. The `too_many_arguments (8/7)` error on `tilted_wall` is resolved by the parameter struct.
- The tests stay in the lowest crate (`camcraft-motion`), the module has its `#3554` provenance line, the file is 203 lines, and there is no `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!`. The body has `Changelog: none` (test-only) and `Fixes #3554`; the subjects are conventional.

**Results merged with main (locally; `origin/main` 4dba7019d; trial merge clean)**
- Build: `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib --no-run` - ok.
- Pinning tests by name - ok, 3 passed:
  - `tilted_wall_builder_at_zero_tilt_is_a_z_hole`
  - `tilted_holes_in_a_plate_are_not_drilled_along_z`
  - `a_tilt_the_fit_accepts_moves_no_wall_past_fit_tol`
- Full touched binary: `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib` - 570 passed, 0 failed, 10 ignored. The count matches the reviewed head; no regression.
- Clippy: `cargo clippy -j 3 -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` - exit 0, no warnings.
- Light lane (`cargo xtask gate light`): `light build (release --no-run)` ok; `motion light: lib` (`the_slot_keeps_its_verdict_under_sub_micron_perturbations_light`) ok; `motion light: adaptive_troch_parallel` (`wide_rectangular_pocket_is_cleared_by_parallel_lanes_light`) ok. 3 steps, 0 failed.

**Targeted tests**
- No post or toolpath change; the example catalog suites are not reached.
- The diff is P1 and test-only. `cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main --dry-run` reaches `motion heavy: every target` and `app heavy: every target` through the one `#[cfg(test)] mod tests_tilted;` line at `crates/motion/src/drilling/mod.rs:73`. The binary that holds the drilling heavy tests is the motion lib. I ran one targeted step: `cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main --only "motion heavy: lib"` - ok in 169 s, 0 failed, 0 stalled. The full heavy lanes do not run for a PR.

**Requested before merge**
- None.

**Questions / notes (not blocking)**
- The PR has no product-code change. It pins an existing refusal; it does not change it. The named skip for a tilted hole stays a follow-up, as the body says.
- The body quotes the mutation and the issue result; both still match the code.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
